limits: Compatibility concerns resolved means/error bars only, not hidden or overlapping pixels.
Source Ns=8 versus exact Ns=9 sector is excluded from the common-conditions global test.
Population SD (ddof=0) and sample SD (ddof=1) are separate declared conventions; the source does not state its ddof. Complex Haar bases and natural logarithms are fixed.
Global tests retain constant-feature mismatches. The audit filtered every previously located marker using the same source-only ring rule; hidden means remain unresolved.
A non-rejection is statistical compatibility, not proof that source and computed arrays are identical.

h2.method: For integer Q and nonnegative represented photon moment p, floor(Q-p)=Q-ceil(p); no subtraction or rounding threshold.
h2.statistical_method: Source marker intervals, including unresolved markers, bound each normalized CDF. A union of two DKW bounds gives a conservative 95% two-sample diagnostic, using the source minimum 475 trajectories.
limits: The sign/size of a tiny numerical photon moment is not a rigorous ODE error certificate. Paired sensitivity is reported separately.
Coherent GS is not assigned a definite Q. Its own coherent ensemble is used.
CDF non-rejection is compatibility; unresolved markers have no finite upper count bound, so most intervals have low power. No arbitrary 180-count ceiling is assumed.
Each displayed 95% DKW comparison is pointwise for one full CDF, not a simultaneous test over all 12 initial-state ensembles.

Source exact trajectory totals, initial cavity state and any finite-precision integer-bin policy are not given. Source-CDF comparisons are conditional on its empirical support lying within the displayed range.

h1.note: At the fixed nominal times: Hermitian weighted candidate 94/94 compatible readings; unweighted norm 0/94. Reading windows are not author confidence intervals.
limits: Source readings are diagnostic pixel intervals, not author arrays or confidence intervals.
Linear interpolation is used over a finite observation time grid; interpolation error is not bounded.
Time-envelope includes source horizontal reading interval and pointwise 2 empirical SE only.
Neither overlapping intervals nor lower RMS establishes unique source operator identity.
Weighted imaginary parts need not vanish; two real part is an explicit Hermitian diagnostic variant.
Original Hamiltonian and jumping process are unchanged; Q-dephased GS is used only for linear Q-invariant means.
